text: SLICE 6 - THE SILENT PRICE DISAPPEARANCE NOW HAS A SIGNAL. SHA 54fc41f7854ca1fb471241c8ffdbd3ffedd21a7c on fable/catalog-action-unification-20260820, based bd3aaad, pushed. YOUR OWN DOC NAMED THIS: the retail reconciliation says an ambiguous price 'silently disappears from every customer surface', the product 'becomes indistinguishable from one that was never priced', and there is 'no error, no log line a customer or an operator would see'. That was still exactly true in code. WIDER THAN AMBIGUITY: price-authority.ts wraps the binding and price reads in a bare catch, so ONE upstream blip turns every price on a catalogue page into Price on request while the page looks healthy - the founder's standing rule is that an upstream blip must not convert valid prices into Price on request. WHAT I CHANGED: nothing about behaviour. Still fail closed, no invented price, no zero. Added an optional onPricingIncident observer on the price authority that fires for price_ambiguous, reader_threw and identity_mismatch, carrying offeringId + offeringVariantId so an operator can find the row. It stays SILENT for a genuinely unpriced variant, because a signal that fires on the ordinary correct case is noise nobody reads - two of the 426 rows are legitimately Price on request. A throwing observer is swallowed. TO ACTIVATE: pass onPricingIncident where you build the price authority; with no observer the behaviour is byte-identical to today, so this is safe to integrate before you decide where the signal should go. WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO, and I think it is yours: MasterOfferingPriceView has two states, so 'could not price' cannot be distinguished from 'not priced' on the wire, and a surface therefore cannot say 'pricing temporarily unavailable' instead of asserting quote-only. I measured before proposing - on_request appears across 46 files and the load-bearing consumers reach into shared/research/launch (s10) and shared/research/storefront, which are being actively written right now. That is a cross-lease contract change and belongs to you after the launch push, not to a worker mid-flight.
